title: Darmiyan
job: Darmiyan's BrainSee is prescription software for doctors. For a person aged 55 to 95 who already has amnestic mild cognitive impairment, it reads a standard brain MRI, age, sex and memory-test scores and returns a score from 0 to 100. A score above 50 looks more like people who developed Alzheimer's dementia within five years, and a score below 50 looks more like people who did not. The FDA says a doctor must not diagnose or decide treatment from this score alone, and the scan needs no contrast dye.
who_pays: Doctors order it. The FDA limits sale and use to prescription, and clinicians upload the MRI through a web portal. No public price is listed.

what_it_does.text: Darmiyan's BrainSee is prescription software for doctors. For a person aged 55 to 95 who already has amnestic mild cognitive impairment, it reads a standard brain MRI, age, sex and memory-test scores and returns a score from 0 to 100. A score above 50 looks more like people who developed Alzheimer's dementia within five years, and a score below 50 looks more like people who did not. The FDA says a doctor must not diagnose or decide treatment from this score alone, and the scan needs no contrast dye.

who_pays.text: Doctors order it. The FDA limits sale and use to prescription, and clinicians upload the MRI through a web portal. No public price is listed.

traction.text: The FDA granted De Novo clearance DEN220066 on 11 January 2024, after a breakthrough designation the company dates to May 2021. In the clearance study, 198 people at 27 North American hospitals were scored against five years of follow-up: specificity was 96.3% and sensitivity was 72.9%. The company said in January 2024 that doctors could use it through a secure web portal. No sales or user count is published.

why_interesting.text: It uses an ordinary MRI a memory clinic may already have, instead of a spinal tap or a PET scan, and it forecasts five years ahead rather than claiming to diagnose Alzheimer's on the spot. The FDA created a new device category for it. The same review notes that the study group was mostly white, that the low end of the sensitivity range sat under the 70% bar the company had set, and that a follow-up study in a wider group of patients was required.

status.text: The company website still presents BrainSee as its first product, with FDA clearance in January 2024. No 2025 or 2026 sales update was found.
